rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads this and the next three verbs in third person, matching the generic singular human understood collectively.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو هذا والثلاثة بعده بياء الغيبة حملا على معنى الإنسان المتقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use second-person forms, addressing generic humanity by a shift in person.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالتاء في الجميع خطابا للإنسان المراد به الجنس على طريق الالتفات

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans read taḥāḍḍūn, eliding one of the two original ta letters; it means that people urge one another.
rows.anchor: فحذف إحدى التاءين، أي: لا يحض بعضكم بعضا.

rows.speaker: الكسائي، زيد بن علي، علقمة
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī is also reported, as are Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿAlqama, to read with a ḍamma on ta, meaning urge yourselves.
rows.anchor: بضم التاء، وهي قراءة زيد ابن علي وعلقمة، أي: تحاضون أنفسكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readers use taḥuḍḍūn, from urging someone; its object is omitted, either yourselves or others, or no object need be supplied.
rows.anchor: من حضه على كذا، أي: أغراه به. ومفعوله محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ʿalā ṭaʿām is governed by taḥāḍḍūn.
rows.anchor: قوله: { على طعام }: متعلق بتحاضون. و

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaʿām may retain its ordinary sense of food, stand for giving or supplying food with an omitted noun, or mean the verbal act of feeding without ellipsis.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون على أصله من كونه اسما للمطعوم. ويكون على حذف مضاف، أي: على بذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ in al-turāth replaces wāw because the word derives from inheritance; tawalluj, tawrāh, and tukhmah are parallels.
rows.anchor: بدل من الواو، لأنه من الوراثة. ومثله: تولج وتوراة وتخمة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lammā means collected together, as in al-Ḥuṭayʾa's example; al-jamm means abundant, with examples for water and hair and the crowd idiom.
rows.anchor:
إذا كان لما يتبع الذم ربه
فلا قدس الرحمن تلك الطواحنا

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha's line uses talummuhu for gathering or joining a companion in disarray, illustrating the root l-m-m.
rows.anchor: ولست بمستبق أخال لا تلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhayr's poem uses jamm for abundant water; the text also mentions abundant hair and the idiom for a great crowd.
rows.anchor: فلما وردن الماء زرقا جمامه

rows.speaker: ابن عصفور
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṣfūr treats the second dakkan as verbal emphasis of the first; the author says this is not the intended sense.
rows.anchor: الثاني تأكيد للأول تأكيدا لفظيا، كذا قاله ابن عصفور، وليس المعنى على ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated dakkan is circumstantial, describing the earth as repeatedly pounded, like learning arithmetic chapter by chapter; this matches al-Zamakhsharī's apparent view.
rows.anchor: أنه نصب على الحال والمعنى: مكررا عليه الدك ك علمته الحساب بابا بابا، وهذا ظاهر قول الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaffan ṣaffan is likewise circumstantial, meaning people standing in rows or in many rows.
rows.anchor: حال أيضا، أي: مصطفين أو ذوي صفوف كثيرة.

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads both verbs in the passive, while the other readers use the active.
rows.anchor: قرأ الكسائي " لا يعذب " و " لا يوثق " مبنيين للمفعول. والباقون قرؤوهما مبنيين للفاعل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Kisāʾī's passive reading, a known but omitted agent is God or the angels assigned to punish by God's command.
rows.anchor: وحذف الفاعل للعلم به وهو الله تعالى أو الزبانية المتولون العذاب بأمر الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verbal nouns may be annexed to the agent, with the pronoun referring to God, or to the recipient, with it referring to the human being; ʿadhāb may mean taʿdhīb and wathāq means īthāq.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون المصدران مضافين للفاعل والضمير لله تعالى، ومضافين للمفعول، والضمير للإنسان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the agent reading, no one punishes this unbeliever as severely as God or chains him as God does; on the recipient reading, none is punished or bound like him for unbelief and defiance.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: لا يعذب أحد تعذيبا مثل تعذيب الله تعالى هذا الكافر، ولا يوثق أحد توثيقا مثل إيثاق الله إياه بالسلاسل والأغلال،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating a verbal noun as its corresponding verb's object is disputed: transmission alternates over whether Basrans or Kufans allow it, and the cited poetry includes ʿaṭāʾ followed by al-miʾata.
rows.anchor: فنقل عن البصريين المنع، وعن الكوفيين الجواز،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also suggests that no one bears another person's punishment, comparing the rule that no burdened soul carries another's burden.
rows.anchor: ولا يحمل عذاب الإنسان أحد كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the active reading, the verbs are assigned to their agents.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة الباقين فإنه أسند الفعل لفاعله.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh takes the pronouns as referring to God: no worldly punishment compares with God's punishment on that Day; the author objects that يومئذ cannot modify a comparison verbal noun placed after it, unless usage is extended.
rows.anchor: كذا قاله أبو عبد الله، وفيه نظر: من حيث إنه يلزم أن يكون " يومئذ " معمولا للمصدر التشبيهي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God leaves neither punishment nor binding to anyone else, since command over both belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لا يكل عذابه ولا وثاقه لأحد؛ لأن الأمر لله وحده في ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed comparison with an unmatched worldly punishment is rejected: the present verb points forward, whereas يومئذ is the Resurrection, not worldly life.
rows.anchor: إذا دخلت على المضارع صيرته مستقبلا، وإذا كان مستقبلا لم يطابق هذا المعنى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading that God punishes an unbeliever in this world as no one else does is rejected by the same objections.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أنه لا يعذب أحد في الدنيا مثل عذاب الله الكافر فيها، إلا أن هذا مردود بما رد به ما قبله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronoun refers to the human being, it can mean no punishing angel matches the punishment of this unbeliever, or that no one bears his punishment, as in the verse on burdens.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل عوده على الإنسان بمعنى: لا يعذب أحد من زبانية العذاب مثل ما يعذبون هذا الكافر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative that no one bears the person's burden is supported with the parallel that no burdened soul bears another's burden.
rows.anchor:
ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى
[فاطر: 18]. وهذه الأوجه صعبة المرام على طالبها

rows.speaker: نافع، أبو جعفر، شيبة
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ in one transmission, Abū Jaʿfar, and, according to one report, Shayba read wathāq with a kasra on wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع في رواية وأبو جعفر وشيبة بخلاف عنهما " وثاقه " بكسر الواو.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading uses feminine vocative yā ayyatuhā; Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads masculine yā ayyuhā, a form otherwise rejected except by the author of al-Badīʿ.
rows.anchor: هذه قراءة العامة " يا أيتها " بتاء التأنيث. وقرأ زيد بن علي " يا أيها " كنداء المذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine form can be defended because ayyuhā does not agree in number with dual or plural addressees, so it need not agree in gender either.
rows.anchor: ولم يجوز ذلك أحد، إلا صاحب " البديع " ، وهذه شاهدة له. وله وجه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāḍiyatan and marḍiyyatan are two simultaneous circumstantial descriptions; one does not necessarily entail the other.
rows.anchor: حالان، أي جامعة بين الوصفين؛ لأنه لا يلزم من أحدهما الآخر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī ʿibādī may mean entering the bodies of God's servants or joining their company.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون: في جسد عبادي ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: في زمرة عبادي.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، جماعة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, and others read the singular ʿabdī, with the singular used generically.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة " في عبدي " والمراد الجنس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first verb takes fī for figurative location, like entering a crowd, whereas the second takes a direct object for actual location; this explanation works if a believer's soul joins God's company.
rows.anchor: وتعدى الفعل الأول ب " في " لأن الظرف ليس بحقيقي نحو: " دخلت في غمار الناس " ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the soul is a spirit ordered into bodies, the locative relation is actual there as well.
rows.anchor: وأما إذا كان المراد بالنفس الروح، وأنها مأمورة بدخولها في الأجساد فالظرفية فيه متحققة أيضا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may interrupt an oath by the city and what follows about human hardship: even someone as sacred as the Prophet is treated as lawful prey in the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: يعني ومن المكابدة أن مثلك على عظم حرمتك يستحل بهذا البلد كما يستحل الصيد في غير الحرم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Alternatively, the oath consoles the Prophet with a promise of future conquest: he will be free to kill and capture in the city, with ḥill meaning lawful.
rows.anchor: وأنت حل به فيما تستقبل تصنع فيه ما تريد من القتل والأسر،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī supports a future sense by comparing the future-oriented wording to the statement that the Prophet will die, and says future events are present to God; the author notes Ibn ʿAṭiyya disputed the claimed consensus that the sūra is Meccan.
rows.anchor: أن السورة بالاتفاق مكية، وأين الهجرة عن وقت نزولها فما بال الفتح؟ وقد ناقشه الشيخ بما لا يتجه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes the clause circumstantial: the city is not sworn by while the Prophet is present, since he deserves an oath more than it does.
rows.anchor: أن الجملة حالية، أي: لا أقسم بهذا البلد وأنت حال بها لعظم قدرك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that the Prophet is being wronged or treated as lawful in the city.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لا أقسم به وأنت مستحل فيه، أي: مستحل أذاك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may mean the person who begets, or be a verbal noun, making the oath by the parent and his act.
rows.anchor: قيل: " ما " بمعنى " من " وقيل: مصدرية. أقسم بالشخص وفعله.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains mā as asking what was born, that is, a child of extraordinary significance, analogizing the wording in 3:36.
rows.anchor: أي: باي شيء وضعت، أي: موضوعا عجيب الشأن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير، عكرمة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr, and ʿIkrima are reported to take mā as negative, with an understood relative: one who did not beget, namely the barren person.
rows.anchor: قال: معناه ابن عباس وتلميذه ابن جبير وعكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqūlu may be an independent clause or a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون مستأنفة، وأن تكون حالا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has lubadan with ḍamma on lām and fatḥa on bāʾ; Abū Jaʿfar doubles bāʾ and is also reported with it unvowelled, while Mujāhid and Ibn Abī al-Zinād use two ḍammas.
rows.anchor: بضم اللام وفتح الباء. وشدد أبو جعفر الباء، وعنه أيضا سكونها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final radical of shafah is deleted; its original form is shafhah, evidenced by diminutive shufayhah and plural shifāh, like one dialect form of sanah.
rows.anchor: الشفة محذوفة اللام، والأصل شفهة، بدليل تصغيرها على شفيهة، وجمعها على شفاه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shāfahtuhu means spoke to him directly without an intermediary, and the word has no sound feminine plural because its broken plural suffices.
rows.anchor: وشافهته، أي: كلمته من غير واسطة، ولا يجمع بالألف والتاء، استغناء بتكسيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-najdayn may be a locative, or require an omitted preposition if it means the two breasts.
rows.anchor: إما ظرف، وإما على حذف الجار إن أريد بهما الثديان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najd originally means the raised neck, or an elevated road; Imruʾ al-Qays's line uses najd for the high Najd of Kabkab, as the region is elevated above Tihāma.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الطريق العالي، كقول امرئ القيس:

rows.speaker: الفراء، الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj say negative lā is rarely used just once with a past verb; here the later phrase about believing can supply the repetition, as in 75:31.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج: " ذكر " لا " مرة واحدة، والعرب لا تكاد تفرد " لا " مع الفعل الماضي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes lā as repeated in meaning: failing to scale the obstacle amounts to failing to free a slave or feed a poor person.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أنه فسر اقتحام العقبة بذلك " قال الشيخ: " ولا يتم له هذا إلا على قراءة " فك " فعلا ماضيا

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The author's interlocutor says al-Zamakhsharī's account works only if fak is read as a past-tense verb.
rows.anchor: ولا يتم له هذا إلا على قراءة " فك " فعلا ماضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, and Ḥafṣ read muʾṣadah with hamza; the rest use wāw, and the same variants occur in Sūrat al-Humaza.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة وحفص بالهمز، والباقون بالواو،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza reading derives from āṣada, to close; it may instead derive from awṣada with wāw hamzated after a ḍamma, as in 38:33.
rows.anchor: فالقراءة الأولى من آصدت الباب، أي: أغلقته أوصده فهو مؤصد.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reports that al-Sūsī, though known to replace such hamza, does not replace it after a ḍamma, reportedly to avoid ambiguity.
rows.anchor: نقل الفراء عن السوسي الذي قاعدته إبدال مثل هذه الهمزة أنه لا يبدل هذه بعد ضمة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors distinct roots for the two readings: hamza from āṣada and wāw from awṣada.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن القراءتين من مادتين: الأولى من آصد يؤصد كأكرم يكرم، والثانية من أوصد يوصد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet's use of mawṣadah means closed, and another poet's muʾṣadan likewise describes a closed door.
rows.anchor:
تحن إلى أجبال مكة ناقتي
ومن دونها أبواب صنعاء موصده

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr disliked the hamza reading and said he wished to cover his ears when his imam pronounced it.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو بكر راوي عاصم يكره الهمزة في هذا الحرف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Abū Bakr seems not to have retained the hamza reading from his teacher, since Ḥafṣ preserves it more reliably, though Abū Bakr was older and highly trusted in hadith.
rows.anchor: وكأنه لم يحفظ عن شيخه إلا ترك الهمز مع حفظ حفص إياه عنه، وهو أضبط لحرفه من أبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlayhim nār may be a fresh sentence, a second predicate, or a single predicate in which ʿalayhim precedes its subject nār; the last is best.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون جملة مستأنفة، وأن تكون خبرا ثانيا، وأن يكون الخبر وحده

rows.speaker: الحسن، مجاهد، أبو عبيدة، ابن جرير
rows.claim: They take mā as a relative pronoun referring to God, and Ibn Jarīr chooses this analysis.
rows.anchor: وإليه ذهب الحسن ومجاهد وأبو عبيدة، واختاره ابن جرير

rows.speaker: الزجاج، المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj and al-Mubarrad take mā as a verbal noun, meaning the building of heaven, on the premise that mā is restricted to nonrational referents.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنها مصدرية، أي: وبناء السماء، وإليه ذهب الزجاج والمبرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A criticism of the verbal-noun reading is that the oath would then be by the acts themselves, although its intended object is their Lord; replies posit an omitted noun or allow oaths by created things.
rows.anchor: واعترض على هذا القول: بأنه يلزم أن يكون القسم بنفس المصادر: بناء السماء وطحو الأرض وتسوية النفس

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects the verbal-noun reading because of the following فألهمها and its effect on coherence; mā is relative and describes the mighty maker who built heaven.
rows.anchor: والوجه أن تكون موصولة، وإنما أوثرت على " من " لإرادة معنى الوصفية كأنه قيل: والسماء والقادر العظيم الذي بناها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that the pronoun in فألهمها refers to God, so the same subject must be understood in بناها; mā is the only available antecedent.
rows.anchor: يعني أن الفاعل في " فألهمها " عائد على الله تعالى فليكن في " بناها " كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors an explicit antecedent over one merely understood from context when choosing what the pronoun refers to.
rows.anchor: إذا دار الأمر بين عوده على ملفوظ به وبين غير ملفوظ به فعوده على الملفوظ به أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says al-Zamakhsharī does not claim mā is an explicit adjective; rather, it can refer to rational beings and convey their attribute, unlike man, as in 4:3.
rows.anchor:
بل مراده أنها تقع على نوع من يعقل، وعلى صفته، ولذلك مثل النحويون ذلك بقوله:
فانكحوا ما طاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite nafs either magnifies one great soul, identified as Adam, or indicates the generality of souls, as in 82:5.
rows.anchor: والتنكير في " نفس ": إما لتعظيمها، أي، نفس عظيمة، وهي نفس آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qad aflaḥa may be the oath's answer, originally la-qad, with lām dropped because the intervening wording is long.
rows.anchor: أنه جواب القسم، والأصل: لقد، وإنما حذفت لطول الكلام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Alternatively, qad aflaḥa is a digression after the inspiration clause, not the oath's answer; the omitted answer predicts God's destruction of Meccans for denying the Messenger as Thamūd denied Ṣāliḥ.
rows.anchor: فالجواب محذوف تقديره: ليدمدمن الله عليهم، أي: على أهل مكة لتكذيبهم رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed omitted oath answer is that the people will surely be resurrected.
rows.anchor: قال معناه الزمخشري، وقدره غيره: لتبعثن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaḥāhā means spread or extended, with two verb forms; it can also mean went away or rose.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم معناه. وفيه لغتان

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: ʿAlqama's line uses ṭaḥā to mean went away or departed.
rows.anchor:
قال علقمة:
4579 طحابك قلب في الحسان طروب
بعيد الشباب عصر حان مشيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent subject of zakāhā and dassāhā is man; an alternative makes God the subject, but the author rejects it as syntactically awkward because the pronoun must refer back through nafs and its possessor.
rows.anchor: والحق أنه خلاف الظاهر، لا لما قال الزمخشري، بل لمنافرة نظمه للاحتياج إلى عود الضمير على النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dassāhā derives from dassasahā; repeated like consonants led the third s to be replaced by a weak letter, as in qaṣaytu.
rows.anchor: أصله دسسها فكثرت الأمثال فأبدل من ثالثها حرف علة كما قالوا: قصيت [أظفاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadsiyah means concealment: the soul was hidden through wickedness; the cited poets retain the unreduced root in their use of dassa.
rows.anchor: والتدسية: الإخفاء بمعنى أخفاها بالفجور، وقد نطق بالأصل من قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet describes having hidden ʿAmr, whose wives were left widowed and abandoned.
rows.anchor:
وأنت الذي دسست عمرا فأصبحت
حلائله منه أرامل ضيعا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī begins with an instrumental, metaphorical bāʾ: Thamūd committed denial by its own overweening transgression.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنها للاستعانة مجازا، كقوله: " كتبت بالقلم " وبه بدأ الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis makes bāʾ causative: they denied what they were threatened with, the punishment of the transgressing blast, as in 69:5.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أنها للتعدية، أي: كذبت بما أوعدت به من عذابها ذي الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis makes bāʾ causal: Thamūd denied because of its transgression.
rows.anchor: والثالث: أنها للسببية، أي: بسبب طغيانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common fatḥ reading ṭaghwāhā is a verbal noun meaning tyranny; yā is changed to wāw in the noun to distinguish it from the adjective.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة " طغواها " بفتح الطاء وهو مصدر بمعنى الطغيان، وإنما قلبت الياء واوا فرقا بين الاسم والصفة

rows.speaker: الحسن، محمد بن كعب، حماد
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, and Ḥammād read with ḍamma on ṭāʾ; this too is a verbal noun but is irregular if the verb is ṭaghaytu.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومحمد بن كعب وحماد بضم الطاء، وهو أيضا مصدر كالرجعى والحسنى، إلا أن هذا شاذ

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says the wāw is original for speakers who use the verb ṭaghawtu rather than ṭaghaytu.
rows.anchor: فالواو أصل عنده، قاله ابو البقاء، وقد تقدم الكلام على اللغتين في البقرة والله الحمد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh may modify either kadhdhabat or al-ṭaghwā.
rows.anchor: يجوز فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يكون ظرفا ل " كذبت " والثاني: أن يكون ظرفا للطغوى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashqāhā may be one particular man, identified in commentary as Qudār ibn Sālif, or a group.
rows.anchor: أن يراد به شخص واحد بعينه. وفي التفسير أنه رجل يسمى قدار بن سالف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī permits the singular superlative form for a group because a definite superlative is invariant across number and gender, though ashqawhā could also have been used.
rows.anchor: وكان ينبغي أن يقيد فيقول: إذا أضفته إلى معرفة؛ لأن المضاف إلى النكرة حكمه الإفراد والتذكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says al-Zamakhsharī should specify that this invariance applies when the superlative is definite; an indefinite or min-governed form is singular masculine anyway.
rows.anchor: وكان ينبغي أن يقيد فيقول: إذا أضفته إلى معرفة؛ لأن المضاف إلى النكرة حكمه الإفراد والتذكير مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ashqāhā denotes a group, lahum refers to them; if it denotes one named man, lahum refers to Thamūd.
rows.anchor: وإن كان المراد به علما بعينه فالضمير من " لهم " يعود على ثمود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāqat Allāh is an accusative warning, meaning beware God's she-camel; the warning verb must be omitted because the construction is coordinated, one of three contexts requiring omission.
rows.anchor: ناقة الله } منصوب على التحذير، أي: احذروا ناقة الله فلا تقربوها، وإضمار الناصب هنا واجب لمكان العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads nāqatu Allāh in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning this is God's she-camel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي " ناقة الله " رفعا على خبر ابتداء مضمر، أي: هذه ناقة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damdama is variously glossed as covering or enclosing, pressing to the ground, utterly destroying, imitating the sound of a collapse, or coating cloth with dye.
rows.anchor: الدمدمة. قيل: الإطباق يقال: دمدمت عليه القبر، أي: أطبقته عليه. وقيل: الإلزاق بالأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in bi-dhanbihim marks cause.
rows.anchor: والباء في " بذنبهم " للسببية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fa-sawwāhā, the object pronoun can refer to Thamūd as a tribe, or to the punishment, leveled among them so none escaped.
rows.anchor: الضمير المنصوب يجوز عوده على ثمود باعتبار القبيلة كما أعاده في قوله " بطغواها

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads fa-dahdama with hāʾ instead of mīm; it has the same meaning as the common reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير " فدهدم " بهاء بين الدالين بدل الميم، وهي بمعنى القراءة المشهورة

rows.speaker: نافع، ابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-lā with fāʾ; other readers use wāw, matching the respective Medina and Syrian codices versus other codices.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر " فلا " بالفاء، والباقون بالواو، ورسمت في مصاحف المدينة والشام بالفاء

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have read wa-lam yakhaf, supporting the wāw reading, as al-Zamakhsharī notes.
rows.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ " ولم يخف " وهي مؤيدة لقراءة الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ conveys sequence; the wāw may mark a circumstantial clause or introduce new information.
rows.anchor: فالفاء تقتضي التعقيب، وهو ظاهر. والواو يجوز أن تكون للحال، وأن تكون لاستئناف الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of yakhāf most likely is the Lord as the closest antecedent; it may instead be the Messenger or ashqāhā, who acts without fearing the outcome.
rows.anchor: ضمير الفاعل في " يخاف " يحتمل عوده على الرب، وهو الأظهر، لكونه أقرب مذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUqbā denotes a thing's end or outcome.
rows.anchor: وعقبى الشيء خاتمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may mean man, following scholars mentioned in the previous sūra, or be a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: يجوز في " ما " أن تكون بمعنى " من " وهو رأي جماعة تقدم ذكرهم في السورة قبلها. وقيل: هي مصدرية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the implied subject as the supremely powerful Creator who formed male and female from one fluid.
rows.anchor: والقادر: العظيم القدرة الذي قدر على خلق الذكر والأنثى من ماء واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reads wa-l-dhakara wa-l-unthā; ʿAbd Allāh reads wa-alladhī khalaqa; and al-Kisāʾī, with Thaʿlab attributing it to some early authorities, reads al-dhakari in the genitive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو الدرداء " والذكر والأنثى " وقرأ عبد الله " والذي خلق " ، والكسائي ونقلها ثعلب عن بعض السلف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains genitive al-dhakari as a substitute for the syntactic position of mā khalaqa, meaning God's creation, with God understood because He alone creates.
rows.anchor: على أنه بدل من محل " ما خلق " بمعنى " وما خلقه " أي: ومخلوق الله الذكر

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The interlocutor instead derives the genitive by imagining a verbal noun construction, as in the cited line's genitive al-rāhib for an implied ṭawāf.
rows.anchor:
وقد يخرج على توهم المصدر، أي: وخلق الذكر، كقوله:
4583 تطوف العفاة بأبوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the poem more likely has the softened nisba form al-rāhibī, as with other rare softened nisba adjectives; he applies this to the line used by Kufans for a fronted subject too.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر في تخريج البيت أن اصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading of tajallā is past tense with al-nahār as subject; ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr reads tatajallā for the sun, and another reading has tajallī with the sun understood and a pronoun referring to day.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة { تجلى } فعلا ماضيا، وفاعله ضمير عائد على النهار. وعبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير " تتجلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bazzī doubles the tāʾ of talazzā; the meeting of two quiescent letters is awkward, like the cited form in 24:15.
rows.anchor: أن البزي يشدد مثل التاء، والتشديد فيها عسر لالتقاء الساكنين فيها على غير حدهما

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ describes a reading with kasra on tanwīn and doubled tāʾ; the author calls it rare but regular because it avoids the forbidden meeting of two quiescent letters.
rows.anchor: يقرأ بكسر التنوين وتشديد التاء، وقد ذكر وجهه عند

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير، سفيان، زيد بن علي، طلحة
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr, Sufyān, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and Ṭalḥa read tatalaẓẓā with two tāʾs, the original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير وسفيان وزيد بن علي وطلحة " تتلظى " بتاءين وهو الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes ashqā and atqā to mean simply wretched and pious, without comparison, since the fire and its avoidance are not exclusive to the most extreme cases.
rows.anchor: قيل: الأشقى والأتقى بمعنى الشقي والتقي ولا تفضيل فيهما؛ لأن النار ليست مختصة بالأكثر شقاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī keeps the comparative force and explains the wording as a balance between an eminent unbeliever and believer, hyperbolically as if the fire and paradise were made for each alone; he identifies them as Abū Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf and Abū Bakr.
rows.anchor: الآية واردة في لموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين، فأريد أن يبالغ في صفتيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tujzā is an adjective of niʿmah, meaning it repays a person; it is passive imperfect for the rhyme, where the underlying construction would have two objects.
rows.anchor: صفة لنعمة، أي: تجزي الإنسان، وإنما جيء به مضارعا مبنيا للمفعول لأجل الفواصل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats ibtighāʾa as a purpose object by sense: wealth is given seeking God's approval, not repayment for a favor.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا له على المعنى؛ لأن المعنى: لا يؤتي ماله إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ similarly paraphrases: I gave not to seek your reward but to seek God's approval.
rows.anchor: ما أعطيتك ابتغاء جزائك، بل ابتغاء وجه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the accusative is a disconnected exception because seeking God's face is outside the class of favors received; this is the common reading.
rows.anchor: أنه منصوب على الاستثناء المنقطع، إذ لم يندرج تحت جنس " من نعمة " وهذه قراءة العامة

rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: Yaḥyā reads ibtighāʾu in the nominative as an appositive to the syntactically nominative min niʿmah; this follows the Tamimi usage of disconnected exceptions in nonaffirmative clauses.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى برفعه ممدودا على البدل من محل " من نعمة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī cites poetry from Bishr ibn Abī Khāzim for the accusative and a second poet for a raised exception.
rows.anchor: وأنشد الزمخشري بالوجهين: النصب والبدل قول بشر بن أبي خازم

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī calls the nominative apposition reading distant; the author replies that he seems unaware it is transmitted and that it is a widespread dialect.
rows.anchor: وقال مكي: " وأجاز الفراء الرفع في " ابتغاء " على البدل من موضع " نعمة " وهو بعيد

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads ibtighāʾ with a shortened final vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن ابي عبلة " ابتغا " بالقصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-la-sawfa yarḍā is the answer to an implicit oath; the common reading is active.
rows.anchor: هذا جواب قسم مضمر. والعامة على " يرضى " مبنيا للفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive reading, meaning God will make him content, is close to the wording at the end of Ṭā Hā.
rows.anchor: وقرئ ببنائه للمفعول من أرضاه الله، وهو قريب من قوله في آخر سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām on wa-la-l-ākhirah is the oath's answer: God swears by four matters, two denials of abandonment and hatred, then the afterlife's superiority and a promise to give satisfaction.
rows.anchor: الظاهر في هذه اللام أنها جواب القسم، وكذلك في " ولسوف " أقسم تعالى على أربعة أشياء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the lām before sawfa as lām of emphasis, supplying a hidden subject, because an oath-lām before a present verb ordinarily requires the emphatic nūn.
rows.anchor: هي لام الابتداء المؤكدة لمضمون الجملة، والمبتدأ محذوف تقديره: ولأنت سوف يعطيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author chooses the oath-lām account, noting the grammar allows omission of emphatic nūn when an interval such as sawfa or a verb object intervenes.
rows.anchor: يختار منه أنها لام القسم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī says this is the lām of an oath such as la-aqūman, not the lām in inna Zaydan la-qāʾim; sawfa substitutes for one emphatic nūn.
rows.anchor: قال الفارسي: " ليست هذه اللام هي التي في قولك:

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The interlocutor first calls the lām on wa-la-l-ākhirah an emphatic lām of beginning, then allows it and the lām on wa-la-sawfa to be oath-lāms coordinated with the oath's answer.
rows.anchor: ويجوز عندي أن تكون اللام في " وللآخرة خير " وفي " ولسوف يعطيك " اللام التي يتلقى بها القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the lām clauses clearly continue the oath answer; a hidden subject after al-Zamakhsharī's analysis does not prevent that function.
rows.anchor: ولا يظهر انقطاع هذه الجملة عن جواب القسم البتة، وكذلك في { ولسوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common āwā is the transitive quadriliteral; Abū al-Ashhab reads the intransitive triliteral awā.
rows.anchor: العامة على " آوى " بألف بعد الهمزة رباعيا، من آواه يؤويه. وأبو الأشهب " فأوى " ثلاثيا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the triliteral may mean the same as sheltered, or mean showed mercy; a shepherd's use is cited for the first and poetry for the second.
rows.anchor: وهو على معنيين: إما من " أواه " بمعنى آواه. سمع بعض الرعاة يقول: " أين آوي هذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shepherd's present-tense āwī proves the triliteral: the quadriliteral would have the form uʾwī; the resulting two hamzas are not merged for weight, as with tuʾwīhi.
rows.anchor: أنه لو كان من الرباعي لقال: " أؤوي " بضم الهمزة الأولى وسكون الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀʾilan means poor; ʿāla means became poor, while a cited line of Jarīr uses al-ʿāʾil for a poor wayfarer.
rows.anchor: أي: فقيرا. وهذه قراءة العامة. يقال: عال زيد أي: افتقر. قال جرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿāla means to have many dependents; the cited verse contrasts when a poor person becomes rich with when a rich person acquires dependents.
rows.anchor:
وأعال: كثر عياله قال:
4596 ومايدري الفقير متى غناه
وما يدري الغني متى يعيل

rows.speaker: اليماني
rows.claim: The Yamani reading is ʿayilan, with a doubled yāʾ under kasra, like sayyid.
rows.anchor: وقرأ اليماني " عيلا " بكسر الياء المشددة كسيد

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik uses al-yatīm preceding lā taqhar to show that an object may precede its governing verb even when the verb follows its jussive particle; the jussive verb itself cannot precede lā.
rows.anchor: وبه استدل الشيخ ابن مالك - رحمه الله - على أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common taqhar is from overcoming; Ibn Masʿūd, al-Shaʿbī, and Ibrāhīm al-Taymī read takhar, from scowling at someone.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة " تقهر " بالقاف من الغلبة. وابن مسعود والشعبي وإبراهيم التيمي بالكاف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī cites the idiom kahara fī wajhihi for scowling and the report that the Prophet never scowled at the speaker.
rows.anchor: يقال: كهر في وجهه، أي: عبس. وفلان ذو كهرورة، أي عابس الوجه. ومنه الحديث

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The interlocutor says the variant has the same meaning as the common reading; the author adds that kahr originally denotes the height of a hot day.
rows.anchor: وهي لغة بمعنى قراءة الجمهور " انتهى. والكهر في الأصل: ارتفاع النهار مع شدة الحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-niʿmati rabbika is governed by ḥaddith, and the preceding fāʾ does not block that relation.
rows.anchor: والفاء غير مانعة من ذلك. وقد تقدم هذا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An interrogative over a negative turns it into an affirmation, meaning God has indeed expanded the Prophet's breast, hence the following past tense; 26:18 is parallel.
rows.anchor: الاستفهام إذا دخل على النفي قرره، فصار المعنى: قد شرحنا، ولذلك عطف عليه الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has the ḥāʾ jussive under lam; Abū Jaʿfar reads it with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: والعامة على جزم الحاء ب " لم " وقرأ أبو جعفر بفتحها.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the apparent fatḥa as a sound produced where ḥāʾ is articulated, causing a listener to think it was vowelled.
rows.anchor: لعلة بين الحاء وأشبعها في مخرجها، فظن السامع أنه فتحها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya posits an original light emphatic nūn after the jussive verb, changed to an alif and then deleted; he cites poetic forms with unexpected fatḥa.
rows.anchor: إن الأصل: ألم نشرحن " بالنون الخفيفة، ثم أبدلها ألفا، ثم حذفها تخفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds this derivation rests on three weak steps: emphasis after lam is rare, nūn becomes alif only at pause, and deleting the alif is itself irregular.
rows.anchor: فتتركب هذه القراءة من ثلاثة أصول كلها ضعيفة؛

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The interlocutor offers a dialect reported by al-Liḥyānī that reverses familiar mood patterns, jussive after lan and subjunctive after lam; he regards it as better than the other explanations.
rows.anchor: وخرجه الشيخ على لغة حكاها اللحياني في " نوادره " عن بعض العرب وهو الجزم ب " لن " ، والنصب ب " لم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anqaḍa ẓahraka compares the burden to a heavy load making the back creak and crack; Arabic speakers use the verb for a camel's back under strain.
rows.anchor: أي: حمله على النقيض وهو صوت الانتقاض والانفكاك لثقله

rows.speaker: العباس بن مرداس
rows.claim: Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās uses anqaḍa ẓahrī for a heavy burden he endured on behalf of his people.
rows.anchor:
وأنقض ظهري ما تطويت منهم
وكنت عليهم مشفقا متحننا

rows.speaker: جميل
rows.claim: Jamīl's line describes ropes breaking with a creaking sound, supporting the sense of naqīḍ.
rows.anchor: وحتى تداعت بالنقيض حباله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has fatḥa on the rāʾ of faraghta; Abū al-Sammāl reads kasra, a dialect al-Zamakhsharī calls inelegant.
rows.anchor: العامة على فتح الراء من " فرغت " وهي الشهيرة، وقرأها أبو السمال مكسورة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī links the command to strive with the preceding blessings and promises: they should prompt gratitude and diligent worship; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as finishing prayer then supplicating.
rows.anchor: لما عدد نعمه السالفة ووعده الآنفة بعثة على الشكر والاجتهاد في العبادة. عن ابن عباس: فإذا فرغت من صلاتك فانصب في الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common fanṣab is an imperative from naṣaba; a doubled-bāʾ reading is attributed to al-inṣibāb, while a kasra-on-ṣād reading is considered suspect.
rows.anchor: والعامة على فتح الصاد وسكون الباء أمرا من النصب وقرئ بتشديد الباء متفوحة أمرا من الأنصباب

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the Shīʿī interpretation of finishing prophethood and appointing a successor weak, anomalous, and unauthenticated from any scholar.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " وهي قراءة ضعيفة شاذة لم تثبت عن عالم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the claim that fanṣab commands appointing ʿAlī an innovation, arguing that a hostile reading could analogously make it command hating him.
rows.anchor: ومن البدع ما روي عن بعض الرافضة أنه قرأ " فانصب " أي: انصب عليا للإمامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farghab derives from desire; Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read faraghghib, commanding people to seek what God has.
rows.anchor: من الرغبة وقرأ زيد بن علي وابن أبي عبلة " فرغب " بتشديد العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭūr means mountain; Sīnīn names the place, so the mountain is annexed to the place where it stands.
rows.anchor: الطور جبل. وسينين: اسم مكان فأضيف الجبل للمكان الذي هو به

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī compares the declension patterns of Sīnūn and Yabrīn, which may take case endings in wāw/yāʾ, retain yāʾ, or vowel their nūn.
rows.anchor: ونحو سينون يبرون في جواز الإعراب بالواو والياء والإقرار على الياء

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ calls Sīnīn a dialectal form of Sīnāʾ.
rows.anchor: هو لغة في سيناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has kasra on sīn; Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, and Abū Rajāʾ use fatḥa, a Bakr and Tamīm dialect.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة بكسر السين. وابن أبي إسحاق وعمرو بن ميمون وأبو رجاء بفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUmar, ʿAbd Allāh, al-Ḥasan, and Ṭalḥa read Sīnāʾ with kasra and length; ʿUmar and Zayd ibn ʿAlī also read the long form with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله والحسن وطلحة " سيناء " بالكسر، والمد

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says sīnīn means a tree and its singular is sīniyyah, a very unusual view not known from exegetes.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: " سينين شجر، الواحدة سينية " وهو غريب جدا غير معروف عن أهل التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-amīn may be an intensive form: it is secure for those within it, humans, birds, and animals; or it may mean trustworthy, since the city protects those who enter.
rows.anchor: هذا فعيل للمبالغة، أي: أمن من فيه، ومن دخله من إنسي وطير وحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis takes amīn as passive: the city is protected from harmful dangers.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى مفعول، من أمنة لأنه مأمون الغوائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is interrogative and nominative as subject, with the following verb as predicate; the addressee is either generic humanity by a shift in address or the Messenger.
rows.anchor: والخبر الفعل بعدها، والمخاطب الإنسان على طريقة الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If humanity is addressed, the sense is: what makes you lie by denying the judgment after the evidence, since denying the resurrection makes one a liar; the bāʾ is causal as in 16:100.
rows.anchor: فأي شيء يضطرك إلى أن تكون كاذبا بسبب الجزاء والباء مثلها في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الفراء، الأخفش
rows.claim: If the Messenger is addressed, the question asks what could make his report of judgment and resurrection false after the signs validating it; al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash give this sense.
rows.anchor: على الثاني يكون المعنى: فماذا الذي يكذبك فيما تخبر به من الجزاء والبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has a quiescent hamza as an imperative from reading; ʿĀṣim in al-Aʿshā's transmission opens rāʾ as if hamza became alif and was deleted in the imperative, with a poetic parallel.
rows.anchor: العامة على سكون الهمزة أمرا من القراءة. وقرأ عاصم في رواية الأعشى براء مفتوحة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes bi-smi as circumstantial: begin by invoking your Lord's name, then recite.
rows.anchor: أن تكون الباء للحال، أي: اقرأ مفتتحا باسم ربك، قل باسم الله، ثم اقرأ، قاله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda offers an extra bāʾ, yielding read the name of your Lord, or treats the name as an added expression meaning remember your Lord.
rows.anchor: قالهما ابو عبيدة. الثالث: أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ may mark seeking aid, with an omitted object: recite what is revealed to you while seeking help through your Lord's name.
rows.anchor: أن الباء للاستعانة والمفعول محذوف تقديره: اقرأ ما يوحى إليك مستعينا باسم ربك.

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash makes bāʾ mean ʿalā, as in ride upon it in God's name, citing 11:41.
rows.anchor:
أنها بمعنى " على " ، أي: اقرأ على اسم ربك كما في قوله:
وقال اركبوا فيها بسم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second khalaqa may explain the first, initially leaving the creation unspecified and then singling out human creation to magnify it.
rows.anchor: ثم فسره ثانيا بخلق الإنسان تفخيما لخلق الإنسان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the first verb omits its object, understood universally as all things, since it is unqualified.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون حذف المفعول من الأول، تقديره: خلق كل شيء لأنه مطلق فيتناول كل مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is specified from among all creation because revelation is addressed to it; al-insān is generic, and alaq is plural because each person comes from a clot.
rows.anchor: تخصيص له بالذكر من بين ما يتناوله الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated khalaqa may be verbal emphasis of the relative clause alone, as in a construction like the one who came, came Zayd.
rows.anchor: فيكون قد أكد الصلة وحدها، كقولك:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about teaching by the pen and teaching humanity resembles create/create humanity, so the same grammatical analyses apply.
rows.anchor: قريب من قوله: " خلق، خلق الإنسان " فلك أن تعيد فيه ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An raʾāhu is purposive: because a person sees himself as self-sufficient; this verb pattern may take two attached pronouns.
rows.anchor: أن " مفعول له، أي: لرؤيته نفسه مستغنيا. وتعدى الفعل هنا إلى ضميريه المتصلين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says seeing here means knowing, since visual raʾā cannot combine two pronouns; istaghnā is the second object.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الرؤية العلم لو كانت بمعنى الإبصار لامتنع في فعلها الجمع بين الضميرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians say visual raʾā can take the construction of cognitive raʾā; ʿĀʾisha's report and a verse about being a target of spears are offered as evidence.
rows.anchor: ذهب جماعة إلى أن " رأى " البصرية تعطي حكم العلمية، وجعل من ذلك قول عائشة - رضي الله عنها

rows.speaker: قنبل
rows.claim: Qunbul is reported with a reading omitting the alif in raʾāhu, a rare contraction; the author says a transmitted reading with a plausible basis should not be called an error, contra Ibn Mujāhid.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبغي ذلك لأنه إذا ثبتت قراءة ولها وجه وإن كان غيره أشهر منه فلا ينبغي أن يقدم على تغليطه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes alladhī yanhā and its conditional clause as the two objects of arāʾayta; the first condition's answer is omitted but inferred from the second, and the middle arāʾayta is emphatic filler.
rows.anchor: الذي ينهى " مع الجملة الشرطية وهما في موضع المفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author analyzes three occurrences of arāʾayta: the third has an explicit interrogative second object and an omitted first; the first and second objects are recovered from parallel occurrences, with both objects omitted from the middle one.
rows.anchor: وهنا " أرأيت " ثلاث مرات، وقد صرح بعد الثالثة منها بجملة استفهامية فتكون في موضع المفعول الثاني لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is deletion licensed by contextual indication, not grammatical competition for objects, because whole clauses cannot be suppressed as individual words are.
rows.anchor: وليس طلب كل من " أرأيت " للجملة الاسمية على سبيل التنازع لأنه يستدعي إضمارا، والجمل لا تضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's proposed conditional answer without fāʾ is not valid; grammarians require fāʾ before an interrogative answer, absent poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: وتجويز الزمخشري وقوع جواب الشرط استفهاما بنفسه لا يجوز، بل نصوا على وجوب ذكر الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At pause, the nūn is represented by alif like tanwīn and deleted after ḍamma or kasra; Abū ʿAmr is reported with emphatic nūn.
rows.anchor: الوقف على هذه النون بالألف، تشبيها لها بالتنوين، وكذلك يحذف بعد الضمة والكسرة وقفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safʿ means seizing, gripping forcefully, and pulling; ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib's word sāfiʿ witnesses that sense.
rows.anchor: والسفع: الأخذ والقبض على الشيء بشدة وجذبه. وقال عمرو بن معد يكرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation derives safʿ from the dark mark on a horse's forelock; al-Rāghib links related words for tripods, an angry person's color, falcon markings, and a dark-complexioned woman to blackness.
rows.anchor: وبه سفعة غضب، اعتبارا بما يعلو من اللون الدخاني وجه من اشتد به الغضب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith describes a woman with safaʿa, darkening on her cheeks.
rows.anchor:
وفي الحديث:
" فقامت امرأة سفعاء الخدين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī justifies the indefinite adjective phrase nāṣiyatin kādhibatin as apposition to a definite noun because its description makes it informative; the author notes this is the Kufan rule, unlike the Basran one.
rows.anchor: وجاز بدلها عن المعرفة وهي نكرة لأنها وصفت فاستقلت بفائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read nāṣiyatan kādhibatan khāṭiʾatan in the accusative as an insult; al-Kisāʾī has a nominative with omitted hiya.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي بنصب " ناصية كاذبة خاطئة " على الشتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the forelock deceitful and sinful is figurative; the definite article may replace annexation or conceal an omitted pronoun meaning his forelock.
rows.anchor: ونسب الكذب والخطأ إليها مجازا. والألف واللام في الناصية قيل: عوض من الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nādiyahu may delete a noun, meaning the people of his council, or figuratively summon the council itself because it contains people, like asking the village in 12:82.
rows.anchor: إما أن يكون حذف مضاف، أي: أهل ناديه أو على التجوز في نداء النادي لاشتماله على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nādī and nadī mean a gathering place for conversation; Zuhayr's reference to councils witnesses the usage.
rows.anchor:
والنادي والندي: المجلس المتخذ للحديث. قال زهير:
4609 وفيهم مقامات حسان وجوههم
وأندية ينتابها القول والفعل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses zabāniya as police; its singular may be zubniya from pushing, or a nisba form zabnī altered from zabānī; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Akhfash give zābin, while others say it has no singular from its form.
rows.anchor: الزبانية في كلام العرب: الشرط، الواحد زبنية كعفرية، من الزبن وهو الدفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root signifies pushing, as a cited poetic line calls warriors zabāniya; war is said to push people, and a customer is a zabūn as he is pushed from vendor to vendor.
rows.anchor:
والحاصل أن المادة تدل على الدفع قال:
4610 مطاعيم في القصوى مطاعين في الوغى
زبانية غلب عظام حلومها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has the majestic plural sanadʿu, written without wāw like yadʿu al-dāʿ; Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads the passive sayudʿā al-zabāniya, with the angels raised as agent.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة " سندع " بنون العظمة ولم ترسم بالواو، وقد تقدم نظيره نحو: " يدع الداع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Qurʾān, omitted because it is known; the night may be a time adjunct for its descent, which commentary says first went to the lowest heaven then to earth piecemeal over twenty years.
rows.anchor: أي: القرآن، أضمر للعلم به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Qurʾān was sent down concerning that night's merit, so the phrase is not temporal; sayings of ʿUmar and ʿĀʾisha use similar wording.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى: أنزل في شأنها وفضلها. فليست ظرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is called al-Qadr either because affairs are decreed during it or because it is crowded with angels.
rows.anchor: وسميت ليلة القدر: إما لتقدير الأمور فيها، وإما لضيقها بالملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-rūḥ may be a nominative subject with the following prepositional phrase as predicate, or an agent coordinated with the angels; fīhā attaches to tanazzalu.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يرتفع " الروح " بالابتداء، والجار بعده الخبر، وأن يرتفع بالفاعلية عطفا على الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-idhni rabbihim may modify tanazzalu or be an omitted circumstantial modifier describing the descending angels.
rows.anchor: المرفوع ب " تنزل " أي ملتبسا بإذن ربهم.

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Min kulli amr can mean for the sake of every matter decreed through the coming year, or by every matter as a transitive complement; Abū Ḥātim gives the latter analysis.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أنها بمعنى الباء، أي: تتنزل بكل أمر، فهي للتعدية، قاله أبو حاتم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، الكلبي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, and al-Kalbī read amriʾ, meaning for each person; interpreting it as every angel is also proposed but called far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وابن عباس وعكرمة والكلبي " امرئ " مذكر امرأة، أي: من أجل كل إنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis attaches min kulli amr to following salām, meaning safe from every fearful matter, but the source salām cannot govern a preceding complement, so an omitted word is needed.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يتم على ظاهره لأن " سلام " مصدر لا يتقدم عليه معموله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If hiya refers to the angels and salām means greeting, they greet every believing man and woman; if it refers to the night and salām means safety, the night is free of fear.
rows.anchor: ضمير الملائكة، و " سلام " بمعنى التسليم، أي: الملائكة ذات تسليم على المؤمنين.

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: The usual parsing puts salām first as predicate and hiya as delayed subject; al-Akhfash also permits salām as subject with hiya its working agent without requiring adjectival dependence.
rows.anchor: فاعل به عند الأخفش، لأنه لا يشترط الاعتماد في عمل الوصف.

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل
rows.claim: Abū al-Faḍl paraphrases hiya salām as safety or a greeting from every matter or person, but the author says the source cannot govern its preceding complement without an omitted element.
rows.anchor:
معناه: هي 

سلام من كل أمر أو امرئ، أي: سالمة أو مسلمة منه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report that Ibn ʿAbbās ended the verse at salām and began hiya as a pointer to the twenty-seventh night is rejected as wordplay that fragments eloquent syntax.
rows.anchor: فلا ينبغي أن يعتقد صحته لأنه إلغاز وتبتير لنظم فصيح الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā maṭlaʿ may attach to tanazzalu or salām, though attachment to the verbal noun is separated by the subject unless the preposition is broadly construed; commentary says angels greet believers until dawn.
rows.anchor: متعلق ب " تنزل " أو ب " سلام " وفيه إشكال للفصل بين المصدر ومعموله بالمبتدأ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads maṭliʿ with kasra on lām, while other readers use fatḥa; fatḥa follows the regular pattern and kasra is attested.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي " مطلع " بكسر اللام، والباقون بفتحها، والفتح هو القياس والكسر سماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians dispute whether both forms are verbal nouns or the fatḥ form is a verbal noun and kasr form denotes a place; the expected pattern has fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وهل هما مصدران أو المفتوح مصدر والمكسور مكان؟ خلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min ahl al-kitāb is an omitted modifier of the subject alladhīna kafarū.
rows.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف، لأنه حال من فاعل " كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common accusative/genitive form al-mushrikīn coordinates with ahl and divides unbelievers into People of the Book and polytheists; a nominative reading coordinates with alladhīna kafarū.
rows.anchor: العامة على قراءة " المشركين " بالياء عطفا على " أهل " قسم الكافرين إلى صنفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author treats munfakkīn as predicate of kāna, with infakka complete here and needing no predicate; another view makes it incomplete with an understood predicate, knowing Muhammad's affair.
rows.anchor: منفكين } خبر يكون. ومنفكين اسم فاعل من انفك. وهي هنا التامة، فلذلك لم يحتج إلى خبر

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The interlocutor says omitting a predicate of kāna is impossible except by ellipsis for necessity, citing poetry.
rows.anchor: وحذف خبر كان [وأخواتها] لا يجوز اقتصارا ولا اختصارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author challenges the interlocutor's logic: both objects of ẓanna can be omitted or one omitted despite serving as predicate and governed object, while omission by اقتصار remains disputed.
rows.anchor: وهذا منتقض بمعفولي " ظن " فإن كلا منهما فيه المعنيان المذكوران، ومع ذلك يحذفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā taʾtiyahum attaches either to lam yakun or to munfakkīn.
rows.anchor: قوله: { حتى تأتيهم }: متعلقة ب " لم يكن " أو ب " منفكين ".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rasūl may be a nominative appositive to al-bayyinah, either apposition of inclusion or whole-to-whole hyperbole, or with an omitted noun meaning the Messenger's proof; it may also predicate an omitted hiya.
rows.anchor: العامة على رفعه بدلا من " البينة ": إما بدل اشتمال، وإما كل من كل على سبيل المبالغة

rows.speaker: عبد الله، أبي
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy read rasūlan in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase from al-bayyinah, preserving the same hyperbole or ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأبي " رسولا " على الحال من البينة

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Min Allāh may modify rasūl or describe it; Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows it to be a circumstantial modifier of the scrolls, understood as sent down from God.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء وجها ثالثا وهو: أن يكون حالا من " صحفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatlu may describe rasūl or be circumstantial to a pronoun in the preceding prepositional phrase if min Allāh is an adjective of rasūl.
rows.anchor: إذا جعلته صفة ل " رسول ".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fīhā kutub may be a full sentence describing the scrolls or circumstantial to the pronoun in muṭahharah; alternatively, only the prepositional phrase is the modifier and kutub is its subject, which is best.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون الوصف أو الحال الجار والمجرور فقط،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common kasra in mukhliṣīn is an active participle governing al-dīn as object; al-Ḥasan's fatḥa makes people purify their own intentions, with al-dīn construed by an omitted preposition or as a cognate object.
rows.anchor: العامة على كسر اللام اسم فاعل، وانتصب به " الدين " والحسن بفتحها على معنى: أنهم يخلصون هم أنفسهم في نياتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhliṣīn is circumstantial to the subject of worship, and ḥunafāʾ is a second circumstance or a circumstance from the first's implicit pronoun.
rows.anchor: حال ثانية أو حال من الحال قبلها، أي: من الضمير المستكن فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command phrase is understood as what they were ordered to do; ʿAbd Allāh reads mā umirū illā an yaʿbudū, that they worship, as discussed with 6:71.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله " وما أمروا إلا أن يعبدوا " أي: بأن يعبدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīn al-qayyimah means the upright community or religion; another reading is the upright scriptures, linked back to the books in 98:3 with a definite article of reference, an analysis praised from Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الكتب القيمة؛ لأنها قد تقدمت في الذكر،

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads al-dīn al-qayyimah; feminine agreement either interprets dīn as millah or uses the emphatic feminine suffix, with poetry offered for the first.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: " وذلك الدين القيمة " ، والتأنيث حينئذ: إما على تأويل الدين بالملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's opening follows the earlier wording; fī nār is its predicate and khālidīn is circumstantial to the hidden pronoun in that predicate.
rows.anchor: و " خالدين " حال من الضمير المستكن في الخبر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Dhakwān read al-barīʾah with hamza in both occurrences; others read the doubled yāʾ form.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن ذكوان " البريئة " بالهمز في الحرفين، والباقون بياء مشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation takes the hamza as original from baraʾa, created; another derives the hamza-less form from al-barāʾ, dust, so the readings have independent roots but one meaning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل البرية دون همزة مشتقة من البرا، وهو التراب، فهي أصل بنفسها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that deriving the hamza-less form from dust would make the hamzated reading erroneous; the author says separate readings may have separate origins and neither mutawātir reading can be weakened.
rows.anchor: يعني أنه إذا قيل بأنها مشتقة من البرا وهو التراب فمن أين يجيء في القراءة الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common khayr is the opposite of sharr; ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid reads khiyār, a collective plural like jiyād and ṭiyāb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة " خير البرية " مقابلا لشر. وعامر بن عبد الواحد " خيار " وهو جمع خير
